contract_inferred: No 00-contract.md. Inferred from the page: web, Persuade (a one-page SaaS landing page for 'Lumina' with nav, hero, logo row, three feature cards and a closing call to action), English only (html lang en at every width), no market named. The URL places it under 'antipattern-examples', so the page may be a deliberate specimen; it is judged here as the layout that ships. No right-to-left language.
overall_reason: The stylesheet has no breakpoints at all, so at 375 the desktop nav and the three-column card grid stay as they are: the page runs to 694px wide and every action label wraps.

score.reason: T-WIDTHS fails at the most common phone width (ROB-010, ROB-007, alongside the sweep's ROB-003 overflow Floor), while T-NO-SCRIPT and T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB pass.

findings.title: The layout holds between and beyond the captured widths
findings.where: Whole page: nav.nav > div.nav-inner and section.features > div.grid, 375px
findings.evidence: The readable stylesheet declares no breakpoints (css.breakpoints_px is empty) and no container queries. At 375 the nav keeps its five links and two actions in one row and the page is 694px wide (parity.document_widths; the sweep's overflow Floor names div.nav-links, 377px). tiles/375-02.png shows the three feature cards still side by side at about 100px each, with the head 'Built to Scale' set one word per line and the body text at three or four words per line.
findings.before: One desktop layout with fixed rows and a three-column grid at every width.
findings.after: Add a phone layout below about 700px: collapse the nav links into a menu, and set the feature grid to repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr)) so the cards stack.
findings.why: A phone visitor gets a page twice the screen's width with feature text squeezed into columns too narrow to read.
findings.root: No responsive rules in the stylesheet

findings.title: Short labels stay whole on one line
findings.where: nav.nav > div.nav-cta > a 'Sign in' and a.pill 'Get started →'; section.hero > div.ctas > a.btn-primary 'Join the waitlist →' and a.btn-ghost 'Watch demo', 375px
findings.evidence: At 375 'Sign in' is 29px wide on 2 lines, 'Get started →' is 84px wide on 3 lines inside a pill that becomes an 85px circle, and both hero buttons ('Join the waitlist →', 161px; 'Watch demo', 134px) wrap to 2 lines (controls.labels_that_wrap). tiles/375-00.png shows 'Sign / in' and 'Get / started / →'.
findings.before: Action labels with no nowrap rule in rows that shrink with the viewport.
findings.after: Give buttons and nav actions white-space: nowrap, and let the hero buttons stack full width below 480px.
findings.why: The main action on the first phone screen reads as three broken lines in a circle.
findings.root: No responsive rules in the stylesheet

strengths: All 834 characters are in the HTML and stay visible with scripts off, with an observer that never fires and with reduced motion.
The page weighs about 1 KiB known over 5 requests, with an LCP of 432 ms in the lab, and uses no images.
At 1280 and 1440 the hero, logo row and cards sit inside one centred column and wrap their text normally (tiles/1440-00.png to tiles/1440-02.png).
not_investigated: T-STRESS: no hostile content was injected; long names were judged from layout evidence.
A right-to-left render and translated strings were not captured.
The page load was not throttled and layout shift was not measured as a number (capture predates the CLS record).
T-FAILURE-PATH and T-SLOW-LINE: async found no primary actions, and no image failed.
T-EXTREME-COUNTS: the page has no counts or lists that take data.
One stylesheet was cross-origin and unreadable; its rules are unknown, not absent. Capture prep blocked /js/detect-antipatterns-browser.js, the host's overlay script.
Widths between the captures, landscape, zoom at 200%, back navigation and deep links.
